metaDescription: Five 12V RV inverter chargers from 1000W to 3000W compared on charger current, transfer switching, battery chemistry settings and installation size.
expertTake: The Renogy 3000W inverter charger is the best pick because it combines a 100A charger, UL 458 safety testing and a slim body for tight bays. The ECO-WORTHY 1000W is the value pick for a small lithium coach. Anyone who only needs AC to DC charging and no inverter should buy a plain converter charger instead.
introParagraphs: An inverter charger does two jobs that would otherwise need two boxes. It also removes a set of cables and a mounting spot from a crowded bay. It makes household power from the battery, and it recharges the battery when shore power or a generator is connected, switching between the two as the situation changes.

The difference between a good one and a frustrating one is rarely the inverter. Charger current, battery chemistry settings and the quality of the transfer switching decide how fast a bank recovers and whether the electronics ride through a power change without a hiccup.

products.name: Renogy 3000W pure sine inverter charger, 100A charger, Bluetooth
products.description:
Passing UL 458 and CSA C22.2 No. 107.1 testing, the safety standards for RV and marine power equipment, is the credential that sets this Renogy apart. Those tests matter on a box that sits beside a mattress or inside a wall. It is described as a three-in-one power solution with a pure sine inverter, a battery charger and UPS backup.

The built-in charger delivers up to 100A, which refills a large lithium bank quickly when shore power or a generator is available. A 300Ah bank takes roughly three to four hours from a deep discharge, depending on the charge profile. The slim 110mm body is designed for tight, space-limited installations, which matters in a coach where bay depth is scarce.

Bluetooth gives you monitoring and settings from a phone. It sits near the top of the price tiers, and the extra cost buys the testing, the charger and the compact design. A 3000W inverter draws about 280A from a 12V bank, so heavy cable and a fuse near the battery are required. For a full-time coach with a lithium bank, it is the most complete solution here.
products.bestFor: Full-time RV owners with a large lithium bank who want certified safety and a slim body.
pros: 100A charger refills a big bank quickly
UL 458 and CSA C22.2 No. 107.1 testing
cons: Near the top of the price tiers
Transfer rating needs checking against your circuit

products.name: Ampinvt 3000W inverter charger, 9000W peak, adjustable 0-35A charging

specList.label: Battery types
specList.value: SLA, AGM, GEL, Li-ion and custom

products.description:
Adjustable charging current is the Ampinvt's strong point. The maximum charge current can be set from 0 to 35A, and setting it to 0A turns charging off entirely. That is useful when a small generator or a weak pedestal cannot supply much power, because you can lower the charger instead of tripping the source.

The unit combines an inverter, a battery charger and an AC auto-transfer switch with a high transfer capability. Battery typesetting lets you choose SLA, AGM, GEL, lithium-ion or a custom profile, with support for LiFePO4, sealed gel, AGM and flooded batteries. A 9000W peak rating is an aggressive surge claim, so read it as a short allowance.

A 35A charger is on the slower side, taking about nine hours to refill 300Ah in theory, so it suits smaller banks or long shore-power stays. It sits at the middle of the price tiers, and an LCD shows what it is doing. If you want a fast charger for generator time, the Renogy is better. For a coach on a weak pedestal, the adjustable current is a smart feature.
products.bestFor: Owners at weak campgrounds or with small generators who want to limit charge current.
pros: Settings for SLA, AGM, GEL, Li-ion and custom profiles
cons: 35A charger is slow for a big bank
Middle price tier with a modest charger

products.name: Redodo 3000W inverter charger, 9000W surge, 45A charger, LCD remote
products.description:
Surge up to 9000W is the number Redodo puts forward, with a 3000W continuous pure sine inverter and a 45A battery charger in one all-in-one unit. A surge of three times the continuous rating is useful for starting a compressor , and the 45A charger is a step above the Ampinvt's 35A. It is compatible with a range of battery types, including gel and AGM.

A remote and an LCD let you see and control the unit. The listing positions the unit as an all-in-one inverter charger, so it replaces a separate converter. That saves a box and a connection, which is where many RV electrical faults start.

It sits at the upper-middle tier. The 45A charger refills 300Ah in about seven hours in theory, so it suits a mid-size bank. The listing does not mention safety testing like the Renogy's UL 458, so look for certification before you buy. For a coach that needs heavy motor starts and a decent charger, it is a good balance.
products.bestFor: Coaches that need strong motor-start surge and a mid-size charger in one box.
pros: Surge up to 9000W for compressor starts
cons: 45A charger is moderate for a big bank

products.name: VEVOR 1200W pure sine inverter charger, 5 working modes, LCD remote

specList.label: Working modes
specList.value: Unattended, AC priority, battery priority, ECO and more

products.description:
Five smart working modes, including unattended, AC priority, battery priority and ECO, are what VEVOR offers beyond a standard inverter charger. They let you decide whether the coach runs from shore power first or from the battery first, and ECO mode lowers idle draw when the load is small. That flexibility helps solar owners use the sun before the grid.

It is a 1200W pure sine unit designed for 12V batteries only, compatible with LiFePO4 and other chemistries. An LCD and a remote make it easy to monitor. The size suits a small coach with a TV, a laptop and a small microwave.

It sits at the lower-middle tier, which is attractive for the feature set. The listing is vague about charger current, so check the manual before you plan a bank around it. It is designed for 12V only, so do not connect it to a 24V system. For a van or small trailer with solar, it is a flexible and affordable choice.
products.bestFor: Van and small-trailer owners with solar who want selectable working modes.
pros: Five working modes including ECO and battery priority
cons: Charger current is vague in the listing
Limited capacity for a full kitchen

products.name: ECO-WORTHY 1000W inverter charger, 55A LiFePO4 charger, 20ms UPS
products.description:
Turning this ECO-WORTHY into a UPS for the coach is its 20 millisecond switchover. When shore power drops, the unit moves to battery power fast enough that most electronics do not notice, which is the behavior a TV and a router want. It combines a 1000W pure sine inverter with a 55A charger designed for LiFePO4 batteries.

That pairing suits a small coach with a modest lithium bank. A 55A charger refills a 200Ah bank in about four hours from empty, depending on the charge profile and the state of charge. The inverter runs a TV, a laptop and a small microwave, though not a heavy kitchen load.

It sits at the lowest tier among the five, which makes it the value pick. Full system protection is listed, and the unit is pure sine. It is not built for the dual legs of a 50 amp coach, so use it on a single circuit or in a smaller RV. Check the transfer switch rating before you connect it. For a van or small trailer with lithium, it is a sensible and inexpensive solution.
products.bestFor: Van and small-trailer owners with a lithium bank who want a low-cost inverter charger.
pros: Lowest price tier of the five
cons: 1000W cannot run a heavy kitchen load
Listing gives little transfer rating detail

buyingCriteria.explanation: Charge time in hours is roughly bank amp-hours divided by charger amps. The Renogy 3000W offers 100A, the ECO-WORTHY 55A, the Redodo 45A and the Ampinvt up to 35A. A 300Ah bank takes about three hours at 100A and about nine at 35A in theory. Match the charger to the bank and to how long you stay plugged in. A short overnight stop at a truck stop gives a charger very little time, so a fast unit matters most when stays are brief.

Lithium and lead acid charge to different voltages and need different float behavior. The ECO-WORTHY is tuned for LiFePO4, the Ampinvt offers SLA, AGM, GEL, Li-ion and custom profiles, and the VEVOR supports LiFePO4 and others. A wrong profile can shorten a battery's life. Lithium wants a defined absorb voltage and no long float, while lead acid wants a float stage to stay topped up.

The changeover between shore power and the battery should be quick and safe. The ECO-WORTHY lists a 20ms switchover, and the Ampinvt has an auto-transfer switch. A unit with no stated transfer behavior is a question for the seller. Never let an inverter back-feed a pedestal. Follow the wiring diagram in the manual and have a qualified person check the work.

UL 458 covers power converters and inverters for vehicles and boats. The Renogy 3000W states UL 458 and CSA testing. The others do not mention certification in their listings. For equipment near a bed or inside a wall, certification is a reason to pay more. It means an outside lab checked the basics of electrical safety.

A weak pedestal or a small generator can trip under a big charger load. The Ampinvt lets you set 0 to 35A, and the VEVOR's ECO mode reduces idle draw. Adjustability protects the source and saves fuel. A generator running well below its limit is quieter and uses less fuel per hour.

The Renogy's 110mm slim body suits tight bays, while the 3000W units overall need a ventilated space. A box that fits the bay is worth more than a slightly better spec on paper. Measure the bay before you buy. Leave a few inches around the case for airflow and for the cables to bend without strain.

specDecoder.watchFor: The Renogy leads at 100A, and the Ampinvt tops out at 35A.

howWeEvaluated.title: Charger capability
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared charger current from 35A on the Ampinvt to 100A on the Renogy and checked profile options. Charger current is the spec that varies most across this lineup. A fast charger earns points for large lithium banks.

howWeEvaluated.title: Safety and certification
howWeEvaluated.description: We credited UL 458 and CSA testing on the Renogy. Certification is a sign that an outside lab looked at the design. We also noted transfer-switch behavior on the ECO-WORTHY and Ampinvt. Units without stated safety details scored lower.

howWeEvaluated.title: Chemistry flexibility
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked how well each unit handles lithium and lead acid. A single profile is acceptable if you only run one chemistry. The Ampinvt and VEVOR offer broad settings and the ECO-WORTHY has a LiFePO4 profile.

howWeEvaluated.title: Installation fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at size and wiring. A unit that fits the bay saves an expensive rebuild. The Renogy's slim body is the easiest to place. The 3000W units all need ventilation and heavy cable.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered monitoring, adjustability and parts support. A unit you can read from a phone is easier to keep healthy. Bluetooth on the Renogy and the LCD remotes on the Redodo and VEVOR help with troubleshooting.

cards.label: Fast charger
cards.text: The Renogy 3000W at 100A refills a big bank in a few hours of generator time. It needs a source that can supply the power, such as a decent generator or a strong pedestal.

cards.label: Adjustable charger
cards.text: The Ampinvt lets you set 0 to 35A, which suits weak pedestals and small generators. It refills slowly but never trips the source.

howToChoose.note: Choose fast for generator charging, adjustable for weak sources.

rows: SLA, AGM, GEL, Li-ion and custom

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A charger current that suits your generator and an adjustable limit if the generator is small. A 100A charger at 14V draws about 1400W from the AC side, so a 2000W generator handles it, while a 35A charger draws about 500W.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Renogy 3000W suits a generator that can supply the power. The Ampinvt's adjustable 0 to 35A suits a small generator that might otherwise overload.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You live in the coach, want certified equipment or have a large bank. The Renogy 3000W provides that.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You have a small bank and light loads. The ECO-WORTHY 1000W and VEVOR 1200W cover them at lower tiers.

maintenance.why: High current heats loose connections. A hot lug is a fire risk, so treat any warmth as a warning. Re-tighten and look for discoloration.
Check that the charge profile matches your battery chemistry. A wrong profile is the most common cause of premature battery wear.
Dust blocks airflow in a basement bay, and a charger section runs warm for hours at a time. Blow the fins out with compressed air rather than wiping them.
Confirm  the unit switches cleanly and isolates inverter output from shore power. Do it with a known load connected so you can watch the changeover.
Corroded holders and chafed insulation add resistance. Wipe the holder and look for green corrosion. Replace as needed.

faq.q: What is an RV inverter charger?
faq.a: A unit that makes AC power from the battery and recharges the battery from shore power or a generator, switching between the two. It replaces a separate inverter and converter. That means fewer boxes to mount and fewer connections to fail.

faq.q: How fast will a charger refill my bank?
faq.a: Roughly bank amp-hours divided by charger amps.  A 100A charger refills 300Ah in about three hours in theory, and a 35A charger in about nine. Real times are longer as charging tapers. The last twenty percent of a charge takes disproportionately long.

faq.q: Can I run lithium batteries on these units?
faq.a: Yes, if the charge profile supports them. The ECO-WORTHY has a LiFePO4 profile, the Ampinvt and VEVOR offer lithium settings and the Renogy handles large lithium banks. Check the manual. Setting the wrong profile can shorten a battery's life.

faq.q: Do I still need a converter?
faq.a: Usually not, because the charger takes over its job. Check that the inverter charger supplies your coach's 12V loads and that the wiring plan covers them. A rewire is usually part of the job.

Most units here include one. The ECO-WORTHY lists a 20ms switchover and the Ampinvt an auto-transfer switch. Confirm the rating against your shore circuit. A switch rated below your circuit will overheat.

faq.q: Can an inverter charger run my air conditioner?
faq.a: A 3000W unit can start a small air conditioner from shore power, but a 12V bank would drain quickly on battery. Most owners run air conditioning only on shore power or a generator. A soft-start kit helps the generator but does not change the battery math.
